limitations: The complete supplied manuscript, source-access note, and bibliography were read. The supplied SHA-256 was treated as an identity label and was not recomputed.

The monetary amounts, procurement dates, and settlement cases are stipulated examples. Their normative conclusions are arguments to assess, not empirical findings independently verified by a source search.

Dorf and Sabel's direct PDF opening initially failed, but opening the independently located search result subsequently returned the author-hosted text. Wallsten's current public article opened successfully; the manuscript's statement about an earlier failed opening is not thereby disproved. Its unspecified archived capture was not available for version comparison.

The care counties, feasible preparations, and three-month transition are expressly hypothetical assumptions. They were not treated as empirical findings requiring external confirmation. The manuscript contains no equations or attributed formal theorems to verify.

The search covered multiple formulations and neighboring literatures but was finite. It cannot establish exhaustive originality, absence of an earlier derivation, or absence of relevant work outside the retrieved material.

citation_audit.evidence: The current [official code](https://www.dhamma.org/en/about/code), Self Discipline & Commitments and Acceptance of the Teacher and the Technique, supports both requirements. Its presentation also supports the attribution of a nonsectarian self-description. Applicability of this wording to the reported 2024 course remains unverified.

The capability answer also requires following instructions and group participation. The manuscript correctly treats this as access to training, not guaranteed enlightenment.

limitations: This was a finite, primarily English-language public-web search conducted on 31 October 2026. Search results establish neither exhaustive originality nor the absence of closer predecessors.

All substantive comparisons below use opened primary texts. Locations_read identifies the portions inspected; availability of a complete source does not mean every page was read. The supplied manuscript and its entire bibliography were read.

Cohen’s article was accessible only as publisher metadata and references. Frangakis and Rubin were accessible only through their publisher abstract and metadata. Neither was treated as a fully examined argumentative predecessor.

Several direct requests failed initially. Search-result opening subsequently provided Buchak’s repository manuscript, Christensen’s paper, and Stilwell’s preprint. These are retrieved public texts, not independently authenticated archival copies.

The current Dhamma pages were checked. Their wording at the particular 2024 Armenian course, the manuscript’s stated access on 17 October 2026, and individual entry assessments were not independently established.
Hovhannisyan’s attendance, health, accommodations, and conversations remain reported events rather than independently corroborated facts. No medical judgment about eligibility or causation was made.

Kent’s and Riebel’s arguments were inspected without independently verifying their historical case narratives. Riebel’s quotation attributed to Watzlawick was not checked against Watzlawick’s original text and is not used to establish that earlier source’s argument.

The public Stilwell record lists May and August 2026 versions. The unversioned retrieved text was compared, but textual identity across those versions was not checked. No inference about V10’s authorship, influence, or borrowing follows.

Alston’s cited précis was checked; his full book was not. Buchak’s substantive section citations were checked, but the bibliography’s ancillary statement about differing final-page pagination across publisher and reprint versions was not fully verified.
